chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'What do you think if she gives birth?' He said, 'It is his child.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَرَأَيْتَ: What do you think? (A common interrogative phrase in hadith)
key_terms.إِنْ حَمَلَتْ: If she gives birth / If she bears

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined in Shia jurisprudence when a woman gives birth?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on marriage details, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the foundational legal principle of *iddah* and paternity, affirming that a child born to a woman is legally attributed to her husband. This ruling serves as the primary evidence for the concept of *iddah* (waiting period) and the presumption of lineage (*nasab*) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring clarity in inheritance and family rights. It underscores the stability of the family unit by linking biological birth directly to marital status unless proven otherwise.
